reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds match the signed batch, but I should verify against the ledger before paying anyone. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are listed. Before paying, I need to verify the refunds against the shared ledger rather than trust the handoff summary, so I'll list the refunds.
The ledger refunds match the handoff exactly: orders 211, 213, and 214, with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
The acme net balance from net_balance is 48125, which matches the ledger (orders 210 and 213 total 63258, less refund 213 of 15133). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 54597 matches the ledger: orders 211 and 214 total 73966, less refunds 12701 and 6668 (19369). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net balance of 46961 matches the ledger: orders 212 and 215 total 46961 with no refunds. All three balances check out against the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 54597 matches the ledger, so I'll record that payout next.
Charlie is the only remaining customer and the last payout to record. Cobalt's net balance was verified as 46961 against the ledger, so I'll record that payout now.

All three customers (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid, and each amount matches the ledger. My previous note mentioned a customer named Charlie, but no Charlie appears in the orders, so there is no fourth payout to make. Finishing the batch now.
